title: Control plane GW NAT translation exhaustion during private upgrade - reconciliation & action items
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a rolling upgrade of the Private control plane in two customer VPC regions, agents experienced intermittent control-plane connectivity loss for 6–18 minutes per region. Root cause was a confluence of (1) an upgrade that changed eBPF conntrack pinning semantics, (2) a new gateway SNAT optimization that reduced ephemeral port reuse, and (3) leader-election churn in the orchestrator which amplified steady-state connection churn. The result was persistent NAT translation exhaustion on the VPC gateway nodes, causing asymmetric flows and session blackholes for control-plane heartbeats and API proxies. Immediate mitigations restored connectivity by switching the gateway pool to a high-ephemeral-mode and rolling back the SNAT optimization in one region. This ticket tracks the follow-ups, remediation, and durable mitigations.

2026-03-01 02:26 UTC: SRE switched gateway pool to high-ephemeral-mode (manual mitigation) — partial recovery observed.

action_items: (A1) Preflight check: add gateway NAT table headroom check to upgrade preflight script; fail upgrade if headroom < 30% (owner: Liam Ortega, ETA: 2026-03-22, estimate: 3)
(A2) Conntrack tuning: propose a default conntrack slab increase for private gateway AMIs and add dynamic slab autoscaling in gateway operator (owner: Priya Sen, ETA: 2026-04-05, estimate: 5)

(A3) Upgrade sequencing: reduce parallelism of gateway+controlplane rolling upgrades; new sequencer to ensure gateway drains + 5m observation window before agent reconnection (owner: Platform Team, ETA: 2026-03-29, estimate: 3)

(A4) SNAT optimization flags: gate experimental SNAT optimizations behind feature-flag & opt-in; add canary probability control on private plane upgrades (owner: Runtime Team, ETA: 2026-03-21, estimate: 2)

(A5) Observability: add per-gateway ephemeral-port utilization metric and alert when >60% consumption; add conntrack eviction rate and drifted-translation-count panels to console (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-28, estimate: 2)

(A6) Automated test: extend upgrade-repro harness to include synthetic leader-election and 10k ephemeral port allocation patterns to catch translation exhaustion regressions (owner: QA, ETA: 2026-03-31, estimate: 4)

(A7) Runbook: update private runbook to include gateway high-ephemeral-mode toggle, rollback steps for SNAT flags, and a checklist for verifying control-plane heartbeats post-upgrade (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-18, estimate: 1)

(A8) Post-deploy dark canary: implement a 10m dark-canary window where a small subset of traffic uses the new SNAT behavior while metrics are evaluated before full rollout (owner: Release Engineering, ETA: 2026-04-09, estimate: 3)

(A9) Customer communication: draft customer incident report and targeted outreach to top-10 affected accounts with mitigation steps and timeline (owner: Customer Success, ETA: 2026-03-15, estimate: 1)

(A10) Long-term: consider per-VPC ephemeral pool isolation or gateway horizontal autoscaling to keep NAT headroom independent of ephemeral reuse patterns (owner: Architecture, ETA: 2026-06-01, estimate: 8)

(A11) Post-deploy validation: require upgrade jobs to run a short live-traffic validation that exercises control-plane heartbeat traffic before completing the job (owner: CI/CD, ETA: 2026-03-24, estimate: 2)

resolution_summary: Immediate rollback of SNAT optimization and manual toggle to high-ephemeral-mode restored control plane connectivity. RCA identified three contributing factors and produced a prioritized action list to prevent recurrence. Short-term mitigations are in flight; longer-term architecture work scheduled.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on A1, A2, A4 during this sprint. Please review PR#1162 and the staging repro; we need sign-off from Security and Networking before enabling any SNAT optimization behind a flag in private regions.
